messages:
kevin: quick follow-up from the console rfc thread — idea to reduce dashboard fanout by materializing heavy tiles and adding a soft-fallback path if materialization lags. sketch below, want pros/cons and rollout concerns.

maria: short version: materialize = precompute tile results and serve from cache/store. fallback = run live query but with stricter timeouts + degraded UI.

jonathan: curious about authz surface — do we materialize per-tenant or store tenant-scoped blobs and authorize at read? storing precomputed rows feels risky for RBAC.

anya: +1 on RBAC question. my vote: materialize tenant-scoped blobs, encrypt at rest, and enforce read-time authz in the console proxy. avoids re-eval on write.

kevin: agreed on tenant-scoped. tradeoffs: storage cost vs repeated compute. also we need freshness guarantees for SLOs. target P95 render ~ 200ms.

maria: two patterns i've seen: 1) materialize-on-write (update tile when upstream events happen) 2) scheduled materialization (cron / windowed). both have different staleness/cost profiles.

jonathan: performance note: materialize-on-write spikes writes but keeps reads cheap. scheduled reduces write coupling but can be stale. if a dashboard has many panels we should allow per-panel policy.

kevin: proposal: per-panel policy with 3 modes: live, schedule (ttl), write-triggered. default = schedule(60s). panels can opt into low-latency write-trigger.

anya: example config snippet:
```
panel_materialization: 
  mode: schedule  # live | schedule | write-trigger
  schedule_sec: 60
  cache_ttl_sec: 65
  encrypt: true
```

maria: fallback behaviour: when a read hits a stale/failed materialization, proxy should try a controlled live query: timebox 300ms, if exceeded return "degraded": true + cached partials if available. UI shows spinner + last-fresh.

jonathan: and about RBAC: do authz at proxy read time. we should store minimal ACL metadata with tile blobs to short-circuit checks (e.g., tenant_id, allowed_roles hash). still enforce at read to be safe.

kevin: cost estimate check: for top 100 dashboards, materialize-on-write increases write ops by ~2x but reduces tokens/compute for reads ~5x. need infra/ops cost vs infra savings.

sre-ops: ops question: how do we handle rollout and failure modes? if materialization service falls over, do we auto-fallback to live queries? that could blow up load.

anya: yes, plan layered fallbacks: 1) if store healthy, serve from store 2) if store delayed, proxy attempts live query with concurrency limit per-tenant 3) if too many live queries, return guarded stale response + error metric. also add circuit-breaker metric.

deploy-bot: deploy notice: materialization-service v0.1 will be deployed to staging tomorrow at 03:30 UTC.

maria: monitoring: add these metrics: materialize_latency_ms, materialize_failures, read_from_store_ratio, live_query_rejection_rate, stale_response_rate. add dashboards for them.

jonathan: security checklist: KMS for blobs, expiry metadata, and ensure indexer never writes cross-tenant keys.

kevin: action items:
- maria: draft per-panel policy UI and default policy text
- jonathan: RBAC read-time design + storing minimal ACL metadata (PR by EOD Fri)
- anya: sketch fallback circuit-breaker thresholds and concurrency caps
- sre-ops: load test staged fallback path and show results next week

maria: +1 will add a short privacy/security blurb for legal review.

kevin: thanks all. if no major objections i'll open a short rfc follow-up with config schema and rollout plan tomorrow. :rocket:
